observations: Timing is the theme of the crates: the opening puts crates inside periodic hazards (flame-jet table, turrets, hatches, fan).
Blue neon arrows are the level's hint language: foreground crate (S4), rail inputs (S6), gem window, phase-waterfall crate (Q-e).
The rail is a transition ride with only 4 crates (vs 26 on 2-1's rails), placed at the neon cue points.
A checkpoint guards a secret: the ! for the gem door sits in the alcove under C3.
The red-gem path holds 24 crates (18%) and about half the Nitros, gated by a gem from another level.
About 8 Nitros sit in an open sand basin as walk-past bait, all counted by the exit detonator.
The bonus is a there-and-back: crates are the floor of the return trip; the pyramid is bounced outbound and eaten inbound.
Support order with explosives recurs: TNT on ? (S1-h), TNT in a floor slot (G-d), TNT dropped onto an iron arrow (P-a).
The phase mask arrives late (C4) for a short vertical finale whose last crate hides in phase effects.
Checkpoints come roughly every 60-90 s of play: after the opening gauntlet, at the branch, after the rail, at the mask, mid-climb.

geometryObservations: Fire is the timing family and it escalates by combination: one sweeping jet with a crate on its table (S1) -> two turrets alternating across a disc line -> one hatch -> two alternating hatches -> canisters at both ends of a bridge with a mutant on it (G) -> a flamethrower on the climb (S9).

Early fire cycles are short (~ 2-3 s) on single hazards; later ones are longer (~ 4-4.5 s) but stacked with other threats (an enemy, a TNT slot, a phase toggle). The window grows as the number of simultaneous problems grows.
Round metal footing shrinks across the level: cog discs ~ 4 u -> 3-4 u -> posts ~ 1.5 u (S4) -> gear stacks ~ 1.5 u (S8) -> 1 u steel and arrow boxes (G, S9). Gap widths stay at 1-2 u throughout.
The red-gem path inverts the moving platform: the disc rotates and carries explosives around a player who stands still.
Explosives become terrain: Nitros as ring corners, a slot in a stepping row and the walls of an arrow shaft (G), then a basin field (S7). The player learns to read Nitros as walls and holes.
Neon signs stand in where the camera cannot help: rail inputs under a chase camera, the foreground detour toward the camera, the gem window, the phase waterfall.

No-stomp enemies (flame helmet, spiked helmet) first appear alone on narrow lanes right after a checkpoint; brutes guard doorways and secrets (gem window, compactor gate); lab minions are fodder placed next to TNT.
A crate-free arena (the junk arena) is a pure hazard test before the bonus: a low sweeper every ~ 2.5 s, cage balls along the sides, a brute in the middle.
The rail is short (~ 13 s), descending and signposted: a transition from the factory to the canyon (4 crates), not a skill test.
Secrets hang off checkpoints: the `!` sits in an alcove under C3's catwalk and needs a slide-jump to return; the red-gem branch starts at C2.
The vertical phase climb is the hardest geometry and comes last, after C4 and C5: phase steps, arrow boxes, a spinning wall gear and rotating spiked wheels. The LP's only death happens here.
Side-on camera for timing rooms (hatches), into-screen for depth and arenas, a side view for vertical climbs: each camera serves the axis of the challenge.
geometryTransfer: Swept deck: a 4 x 3 crate (4.6 x 3.5 m) table with a `firetiki` jet sweeping every ~ 2 s and one crate on it. On foot the player waits behind the sweep; on the board at 12 m/s the deck is crossed in ~ 0.3-0.4 s.
Alternating pair: two `firetiki` hatches 4-6 m apart with a 4.5 s period, offset 2.25 s, and a 2-stack of crates between them that has to come down inside one ~ 2 s window.
Shrinking round footing: discs 4.6 m -> posts 1.7 m -> gear stacks 1.7 m, with gaps of 1.2-2.3 m. Foot only; our full jump spans ~ 5.6 m, so the challenge is the landing size, not the distance.
Signposted descending rail: ~ 13 s (~ 160-200 m at 12-15 m/s) with 2-3 segment gaps of 3-5 m, each cued by a red up-arrow sign 3-5 m before the take-off and a blue down-arrow before any low obstacle.
Crate-free arena test: a floor ~ 9 m wide and >= 14 m long with a `spinbridge` or `pendulum` sweeper at ~ 2.5 s, two `stone` balls rolling along the edges and a `charger` down the middle.
Checkpoint secret: a `bang` switch in an alcove 2.3 m below the checkpoint ledge front, returning by a 2.3 m step-up that needs the double jump (our stand-in for the slide-jump).
